newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP year minerals profit falls 46.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: BHP year minerals profit falls 46.4 pct.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Friday profits including abnormals from its minerals division fell 46.4 percent in the year to May 31 to A$236 million.
The profit for the year from minerals, excluding abnormal items, was A$425 million, a decrease of A$15 million, or 3.4 percent below the profit for the previous year, BHP said.
BHP said the result was achieved despite a higher Australian dollar-to U.S.-dollar exchange rate, which reduced the result by A$74 million versus the previous year.

Record shipments of iron ore from the Western Australia operations, up eight percent year-on-year and only partly offset by the currency exchange rates, and records coal shipments from Queensland, Indonesia and New Mexico, contributed to the minerals division's results, the company said.
However, the benefits of higher U.S. prices for high-quality coking coal was more than offset by the effect of the exchange rate and higher operating costs, BHP said.
Shipments of manganese ore for the year were down five percent at 1.4 million tonnes.
"Higher operating costs together with the effect of the higher A$/US$ exchange rate and sharply lower alloy prices more than offset the benefit of higher ore prices," BHP said.

A net loss of A$19 million against a 1995/96 profit of A$9 million profit was linked to sales of properties within the minerals division and the write-down of the electrolytic manganese dioxide operation in Newcastle, New South Wales to "realisable value," BHP said.
The provision for loss on sale of the manganese operation was A$49 million, the company said.
The loss reported in the November 1996 half year on the sale of the Mali gold assets was reduced by A$21 million due to finalisation of the sale consideration, BHP said.
BHP said it spent A$181 million on exploration and evaluation work during the year, up from A$170 million the previous year.
The charge against profit was A$180 million versus $150 million a year earlier, BHP said.
An abnormal loss of A$189 million in the latest result represents a write-down of assets to recoverable amount following a strategic review of assets, BHP said.
